text: SIGPLAN is the Association for Computing Machinery's Special Interest Group (SIG) on programming languages, focusing on programming language concepts and tools across design, implementation, practice, and theory. Its members include programming language developers, educators, implementers, researchers, theoreticians, and users. SIGPLAN recognizes an individual or individuals who have made a significant and lasting contribution to the field of programming languages. It also honors outstanding contributions by young researchers in programming languages, with the award named after computer scientist Robin Milner. Additionally, it awards an institution or individual(s) for the development of a software system that has had a significant impact on programming language research, implementations, and tools. The John C. Reynolds Doctoral Dissertation Award, named after computer scientist John C. Reynolds, is presented annually to the author of the outstanding doctoral dissertation in programming languages. This award is given to the authors of a paper presented at PLDI 10 years prior to the award year, in recognition of its influence over the past decade, and similarly, to the authors of a paper presented at POPL 10 years prior to the award year, in recognition of its influence over the past decade.
